Model-independent, database-flexible, designed for people and AI agents.

senses: The coordinated and harmonious integration of multiple systems, components, or processes that function as a unified whole.
(Figurative) A complex and elegant arrangement of interconnected parts operating seamlessly, like a symphony orchestra.
definition.modernHtml: A tool-centric cognitive architecture built around one idea: everything is a tool. A single MCP layer allows people and agents to invoke tools to generate interfaces, compose workflows, query knowledge and databases, and perform semantic search. Model-independent (OpenRouter, Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, or any endpoint compatible with the integration) and database-flexible (SQLite, MongoDB, PostgreSQL).

about.heading: About · Everything is a tool
paragraphsHtml: Sysphony moves beyond the chatbot paradigm. At its core is an Model Context Protocol (MCP) aggregator: it connects MCP servers and makes every capability a tool. Tools are not a box in the diagram: they are the connections themselves, the means through which the system operates. Generative UI, a workflow, a database, a knowledge base: each is reached as a tool.

Because everything is a tool, the user can reach them directly: execute a workflow, query a database, access a knowledge base, or drive the UI. The same tools can perform different tasks depending on how they are configured. Nothing is a special case: the system grows in capability without multiplying paradigms.

The AI works through a router agent: the router analyzes the task and selects the most appropriate sub-agents. Each sub-agent operates through one or more domains, which provide access to specific resources, knowledge, or tools. Sub-agents and domains are distinct, composable entities: a domain can be shared by multiple sub-agents, while a sub-agent can use multiple domains (AI → router agent → sub-agent → domain → tools). This separation makes the architecture modular: agents define behavior and operational context, while domains encapsulate reusable capabilities and resources. A tool action can also close the loop: a WebSocket event emitted by a tool can wake the agent, allowing the system to react autonomously to events.

Under the hood: an Express + WebSocket core that scales through role separation: a state server for persistence and real-time events, and stateless compute nodes for executing tools and agents. It works with MCP clients such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, Kiro, and any compatible client. From single-node mode to a full cluster on AWS, the same Docker image can be deployed anywhere.

model.heading: The model · Everything is a tool: the edges are the tools

panelDefault.title: Tools are the connections
panelDefault.descHtml: Every arrow represents a tool. The user directly reaches every final node; the AI passes through a router agent → sub-agents → domains; and a tool action (WebSocket) can return to wake the agent. Hover over (or tap) a node.

model.note: The user calls the tools directly; the AI reaches them through its router and domains; and a WebSocket event can wake the agent, closing the loop.

user.title: The user reaches every tool directly
user.desc: UI, workflow, database, knowledge: sono tutti tools, quindi l'user può usarli direttamente. Gli archi qui SONO i tools.

ai.title: AI works through a router
ai.desc: The agent connects to its router, which selects the appropriate sub-agents. Sub-agents and domains are distinct entities: sub-agents use one or more domains, and domains can be shared across multiple sub-agents.

ui.title: UI is a tool
ui.desc: Generating, rendering, and reshaping the interface is a tool call. The user sees it; the AI can build or modify it: the same tool for both.

wf.title: A workflow is a tool
wf.desc: Compose tools into a graph of nodes with branches and parallel steps; the entire workflow becomes a callable tool with an automatically generated schema.

db.title: A database is a tool
db.desc: Query, read, and write to SQLite, MongoDB, or PostgreSQL, all through a single tool interface.

know.title: Knowledge is a tool
know.desc: Datasets loaded into knowledge bases and indexed for text and meaning. Hybrid retrieval, based on keywords and vector search, is exposed as a tool and feeds RAG.

d-wf.title: Domain over a workflow
d-wf.desc: An expert constrained to a single workflow: it knows how and when to execute that tool on behalf of the sub-agent using it.

d-kb.title: Domain over a knowledge base
d-kb.desc: An expert specialized in a knowledge base: its sources point to that dataset and its semantic index. A domain combines tools and knowledge to perform its task.

router.title: The router reaches sub-agents
router.desc: The router agent classifies each request and routes it to the appropriate sub-agent. Each sub-agent can use one or more domains, and the same domain can be shared across multiple sub-agents.

ws.title: A tool can wake the agent
ws.desc: WebSocket is one of the event mechanisms available to tools: a tool emits a WS event that returns to the system and can wake the AI, closing the loop and allowing the system to react autonomously.

mcps.title: Connect external MCP servers
mcps.desc: Workflows can also connect to external MCP servers: the tools exposed by those servers enter the graph and become composable with everything else.

capabilities.heading: Core capabilities · The tools layer in action

cards.title: Foundation · MCP federation
cards.html: It all starts from a single MCP aggregator: memory, workflow, browser automation (Stagehand), fetch, search, and agent invocation are already built-in tools. Connect any external MCP server and its capabilities join the same registry, callable by humans and agents alike: one access point to everything. See the MCP specification.

cards.title: Compose · Workflows and generative UI
cards.html: If every capability is a tool, you can compose it. Chain tools into a visual workflow, with conditional branches and parallel steps: the whole graph becomes a callable tool with an auto-generated schema (on React Flow). The same logic applies to the interface: agents discover components, create new ones, and reshape layouts in real time. JSON in → UI out, with no redesign each time.

cards.title: Data · Knowledge, databases and semantic search
cards.html: Data is the fuel of agents, so it too is a tool. Query SQLite, MongoDB, and PostgreSQL through one interface, and load datasets into knowledge domains indexed for full-text and meaning. On top runs a hybrid keyword + vector retrieval, with embeddings stored in the database itself: the basis of RAG for every agent and workflow.

cards.title: Experts · Domains and MoE-RAG agents
cards.html: Around each resource (tool, workflow, database, or knowledge base) you can create a domain: an expert constrained to that resource, with its own sources, memory, and tasks. An agent is then a mixture-of-experts, a router plus the domains that compose it, and the router routes each request to the right expert. Domains are composable: one domain serves many agents and an agent holds many domains. Add a resource, get a domain, reuse it anywhere, with no duplication.

cards.title: Runtime · Model-independent and real-time events
cards.html: Execution is not tied to any provider: OpenRouter, Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, or local models, as long as the runtime supports that model or endpoint. While tools run, WebSocket channels stream execution events, tool activity, agent messages, and app state: the compute → state relay keeps UI and agents always in sync.

cards.title: Deploy · Client-independent and cluster-ready
cards.html: As an MCP server, it works with Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, Kiro, and other compatible MCP clients. The same Docker image goes from a local machine to a cluster scaled on AWS ECS Fargate, with peer registration via HMAC.

notes.heading: FAQ · why it is built this way
notes.intro: The questions I asked myself while building Sysphony, and the reasoning behind each choice, without beating around the bush.

items.title: Why tool-centric, with a single interface?
items.html: In years of programming I have seen functions get lost, duplicated, and disappear into the ether of libraries. MCPs instead provide a registry of reusable tools, natively callable by AI as well. Hence a multi-MCP structure: MCP servers dedicated to specific projects, with workflows composed of internal and external MCPs. A kind of inception, where tools create projects and other tools, and then execute them: without writing code, through configuration. What was needed was a uniform system usable in the same way by people and agents.

items.title: In what sense are workflows tools?
items.html: Composing tools to create «complex tools» is the key to sub-MCPs: give an agent a specific MCP and you limit its area of action and knowledge. A workflow is not just a tool: it has object nodes (which define the schema), agent nodes (inputs such as context, lateral tools, and typed output), and condition nodes for branching execution. Edges connect specific values from input/output schemas and handle lists, map, and foreach over arrays, making parallel batch execution straightforward. Each workflow can have cron and WebSocket triggers and a per-step history: complete debugging and logs.

items.title: Why should the UI be generative?
items.html: The internet is changing: traditional websites risk becoming increasingly rigid interfaces compared with what agents can do. What matters is information and action, and the UI should be generated from data and from the interests of the person using it. Why give everyone the same panel with a thousand buttons? Someone who lives in Excel can have an Excel-style UI; someone who wants more can build their own panel, with or without an agent's help. And generative UI lets the agent show you the data: no longer just a chat, but an interface that the AI composes and adapts proactively.

items.title: How do knowledge and semantic search work?
items.html: Working with many agents and large amounts of data, the problem is retrieving the right information across different topics: context is the heart of an agent, the foundation of its continuity and operation. Since everything passes from the memory tool to the database server, I built a simple way to create and manage new DBs, adding chunking and vectorization to the most important ones, so knowledge tools remain reliable and focused.

items.title: What is the MoE-RAG router, and why domains instead of a single agent?
items.html: I do not want to have to reinitialize a session for every task. A context that grows indefinitely can saturate the agent: higher cost, lower precision, and sessions that become difficult to manage. The answer is a mixture-of-experts: a lightweight, always-fresh router agent (each call is a new session, but with persistent base context) that observes state and task, selects the appropriate sub-agents, and lets them operate through their assigned domains. Sub-agents and domains are distinct, reusable entities: a sub-agent can use one or more domains, while the same domain can be shared by multiple sub-agents. The router can query the knowledge of other experts, invoke them, emit events, and talk to the user. It is not a chat: it is context-based continuity, written in the background by other agents, filtered, and ready to explore. The router can write directives, create new sub-agents and domains, and schedule its own execution over time. Domains are specializations (database, knowledge, tools, sites) that sub-agents can compose as needed. The entity is the binary, the model is the carriage.

items.title: Is it tied to a specific provider or model?
items.html: No, it is an architectural requirement: no dependency on a single provider. As an MCP server, it can work with local or third-party MCP clients and, depending on the runtime and integration, with different models and providers. The tools layer remains independent of the underlying model. Thanks to WebSocket triggers, the router also gains a temporal dimension: it can schedule future self-executing events, pause, and, when awakened, check the state of jobs, tasks, and agents.
